newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF tax revenue experts start work in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: IMF tax revenue experts start work in Moscow.

text.p: A group of experts from the International Monetary Fund studying the level of tax revenue started work in Moscow on Monday, a senior IMF official said.

Tom Wolf, head of the fund's representative office in Moscow, told Reuters the experts had started work in advance of a fund mission which would arrive on Thursday for a regular monthly monitoring of the Russian economy.
The mission will be headed by IMF official Yusuke Horiguchi, who arrived with the experts on Sunday and was due to meet Finance Minister Alexander Livshits on Monday.
Last month a fund mission left Moscow postponing a decision on whether to recommend paying out the latest $330 million tranche of Russia's $10 billion Extended Fund Facility.

The mission was concerned at the impact on fiscal policy of the low level of tax collection. Officials say the level of tax revenus rose in the middle of last month as the government put pressure on large corporate tax debtors to pay up.
